summary: This document defines three RTCP Extended Report blocks that report summary statistics on loss, duplication, and discard, for use in a range of RTP applications.

plainLanguage.summary: These are three summary report cards counting lost, doubled, and thrown-away packets.

questions: what is burst gap loss rate
what is frame impairment statistics summary block
subtitle: Three RTCP report blocks that boil packet loss, discard and video frame damage down to a few summary numbers.

tldr.problem: Operators and applications that send real-time media need compact statistics about how loss, discards and damaged video frames are affecting a stream, beyond a single running loss count.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines three RTCP Extended Report blocks: Burst/Gap Loss Summary Statistics (type 17), Burst/Gap Discard Summary Statistics (type 18) and Frame Impairment Statistics Summary (type 19). Each reports fixed-size fields from the receiver.
tldr.outcome: Senders and monitoring systems can judge user experience and adjust strategy. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 7004 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2013. Neither obsoleted nor updated by any other RFC in the metadata, it remains the definition of these three blocks.

sections.title: Three Blocks for Summary Statistics
sections.content:
RFC 7004 adds three new block types to the RTCP Extended Report (XR) framework from RFC 3611. XR blocks let an RTP receiver send measurements back using the reporting scheme of RFC 3550.

The first two blocks report burst/gap loss and discard summary statistics: the proportion of packets lost or discarded, plus mean and variance. They are transport-related end-system metrics. They are meant to be used together with the Burst/Gap Loss Metrics Block (RFC 6958) and the Burst/Gap Discard Metrics Block (RFC 7003), so they depend on those blocks.

The third block reports detailed video statistics per frame type and is an application-level metric. The RFC says these metrics suit a wide range of RTP applications, reflect transient IP problems that affect user experience, and can feed quality-of-experience assessment and sender strategies.
sections.plainLanguage: Think of a school report card with three boxes. One box is about packets that went missing, one is about packets that were thrown out, and one is about damaged video pictures.

sections.title: Frame Types and Interval Flags
sections.content:
The RFC defines one new term, frame type. A video frame can be compressed in different ways. A Key frame is coded independently, without prediction from other pictures, and is used as a reference for predicting others. Derived frames are predictively coded from a Key frame. If there is no video compression, all frames are Key frames.

The loss and discard blocks carry a 2-bit Interval Metric flag (I). Value 10 means the figure covers the most recent interval between reports. Value 11 means it is cumulative. Value 01 means a sampled instantaneous value. The value 00 is reserved and MUST NOT be used.
sections.plainLanguage: A key frame is a full photo. A derived frame is a note saying what changed since the photo. The flag says whether a number covers the last stretch of time, the whole call so far, or just one instant.

sections.title: Burst/Gap Loss Summary Statistics Block
sections.content:
This block (BT=17) extends the loss and discard metrics of Section 4.7.1 of RFC 3611. It has a Block Length of 3 and four 16-bit fields:

  • Burst Loss Rate: the fraction of packets lost during bursts since the start of reception, as a fixed-point number with the binary point right after the left-most bit. It is Packets Lost in Bursts divided by Total Packets Expected in Bursts, times 32768 (0x8000), integer part only. The maximum is thus 0x8000.
  • Gap Loss Rate: the same idea for packets lost during gaps.
  • Burst Duration Mean: the sum of burst durations divided by the number of bursts, taken from the Burst/Gap Loss Metrics Block.
  • Burst Duration Variance: computed from the sum of squares of burst durations, the number of bursts and the mean.

If a measurement is unavailable, the value 0xFFFF MUST be reported. The block relies on the Measurement Information Block (RFC 6776) for the span of the report and SHOULD be sent in the same compound RTCP packet. If that measurement period does not arrive in the same compound packet, the block MUST be discarded.
sections.plainLanguage: Packets often go missing in clumps, like several raindrops hitting you at once. This card says how bad the clumps were, how bad the quiet times between clumps were, and how long a clump usually lasts.

sections.title: Burst/Gap Discard Summary Statistics Block
sections.content:
This block (BT=18) has a Block Length of 2 and two 16-bit fields, Burst Discard Rate and Gap Discard Rate. They use the same fixed-point scheme as the loss rates, scaled by 32768 (0x8000), but count packets discarded instead of lost. Unavailable measurements are reported as 0xFFFF.

For the gap figure, the number of packets discarded comes from the Discard Count Block (RFC 7002), filled with the sum of packets discarded for early arrival (DT=1) and late arrival (DT=2). To make the block meaningful, two instances of the Discard Count Block, with DT=1 and DT=2, MUST be in the same RTCP XR packet. The burst-related inputs come from the metrics defined in RFC 7003.

As with the loss block, this block relies on the Measurement Information Block, SHOULD travel in the same compound RTCP packet, and MUST be discarded if the measurement period is not received in it.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes a receiver throws packets away because they came too early or too late. This card says how many were tossed during the clumpy bad times and how many during the calm times.

sections.title: Frame Impairment Statistics Summary Block
sections.content:
This block (BT=19) extends the statistics summary report of Section 4.6 of RFC 3611 to show which frame types were affected. It has a Block Length of 6. After the standard header and SSRC come begin_seq and end_seq, which define the sequence number interval, and four 32-bit counters:

  • discarded_frames: frames discarded in the interval.
  • dup_frames: duplicate frames received.
  • full_lost_frames: frames where the whole frame, or all its packets, were lost.
  • partial_lost_frames: frames split across several packets where only some packets were lost.

A 1-bit field T says whether the counts are for Key frames (0) or Derived frames (1). If both are reported, they should be sent in the same RTCP compound packet using two blocks. The counts can be inferred from the packets that make up each frame.
sections.plainLanguage: A video picture can be sent in several packets. If all of them vanish, the picture is fully lost. If only some vanish, it is partly lost. This card counts each kind, separately for full photos and for change notes.

sections.title: SDP Signaling
sections.content:
The blocks can be announced in the Session Description Protocol using the rtcp-xr attribute from RFC 3611. The RFC adds three new xr-format values: burst-gap-loss-stat, burst-gap-discard-stat and frame-impairment-stat. XR blocks MAY also be used without prior signaling.

In offer/answer use, the rules from RFC 3611 for unilateral rtcp-xr parameters apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Before a call, each side can say which report cards it is willing to use. Each card has a short name so both sides agree.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The RFC assigns three block type values in the RTCP XR Block Type Registry: BGLSS (17, Burst/Gap Loss Summary Statistics Block), BGDSS (18, Burst/Gap Discard Summary Statistics Block) and FISS (19, Frame Impairment Statistics Summary Block). It also registers the three SDP parameter names listed above in the XR SDP parameters registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Each report card gets an official number, 17, 18 or 19, in a public list so nobody else uses the same number for something different.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that the new RTCP XR blocks do not introduce any new security considerations beyond those described in RFC 3611. Implementers should therefore follow that document's security guidance.
sections.plainLanguage: These cards do not open any new doors for trouble beyond the ones the older report system already had.

fields.name: BT
fields.desc: Block type, the constant 17.

fields.name: I
fields.desc: Interval Metric flag: 10 interval, 11 cumulative, 01 sampled.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero and ignored by the receiver.

fields.name: Block Length
fields.desc: The constant 3.

fields.name: SSRC of Source
fields.desc: As defined in Section 4.1 of RFC 3611.

fields.name: Burst Loss Rate
fields.desc: Fraction of packets lost during bursts, scaled by 0x8000.

fields.name: Gap Loss Rate
fields.desc: Fraction of packets lost during gaps, scaled by 0x8000.

fields.name: Burst Duration Mean
fields.desc: Sum of burst durations divided by number of bursts.

fields.name: Burst Duration Variance
fields.desc: Variance of the burst duration.

fields.name: BT
fields.desc: Block type, the constant 18.

fields.name: I
fields.desc: Interval Metric flag: 10 interval, 11 cumulative, 01 sampled.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero and ignored by the receiver.

fields.name: Block Length
fields.desc: The constant 2.

fields.name: SSRC of Source
fields.desc: As defined in Section 4.1 of RFC 3611.

fields.name: Burst Discard Rate
fields.desc: Fraction of packets discarded during bursts, scaled by 0x8000.

fields.name: Gap Discard Rate
fields.desc: Fraction of packets discarded during gaps, scaled by 0x8000.

fields.name: BT
fields.desc: Block type, the constant 19.

fields.name: T
fields.desc: 0 for Key frame counts, 1 for Derived frame counts.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero and ignored by the receiver.

fields.name: Block Length
fields.desc: The constant 6.

fields.name: SSRC of Source
fields.desc: As defined in Section 4.1 of RFC 3611.

fields.name: begin_seq
fields.desc: Start of the sequence number interval.

fields.name: end_seq
fields.desc: End of the sequence number interval.

fields.name: discarded_frames
fields.desc: Frames discarded in the interval.

fields.name: dup_frames
fields.desc: Duplicate frames received in the interval.

fields.name: full_lost_frames
fields.desc: Frames lost entirely.

fields.name: partial_lost_frames
fields.desc: Frames with only some packets lost.
